summary.title: Recurrent Interpolants for Probabilistic Time Series Prediction
summary.authors: Yu Chen, Marin Biloš, Sarthak Mittal, Wei Deng, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider
summary.executive_summary: This paper addresses the scalability and distribution modeling challenges in probabilistic time series forecasting by proposing a novel framework that blends recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with stochastic interpolants (SI). While autoregressive models like RNNs and transformers are efficient, they struggle with high-dimensional complex distributions. Conversely, generative models like diffusion and flow-based methods offer superior distribution modeling but suffer from high computational costs. The authors extend the theory of stochastic interpolants to a conditional generation framework, using an RNN to encode historical context as a prompt for the SI module. This approach allows the model to efficiently transport the current time point's distribution to the future time point's distribution, conditioned on the history. Experiments on synthetic datasets and real-world multivariate time series (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki) demonstrate that this method outperforms or matches baselines including DDPM, SGM, Flow Matching, and Vec-LSTM, particularly in capturing uncertainty and modeling complex dependencies. The study highlights the effectiveness of SI in balancing computational efficiency with high-quality probabilistic modeling.

claims.description: Stochastic Interpolants combined with RNNs provide a computationally efficient and high-quality framework for probabilistic time series forecasting.
The proposed framework effectively extends stochastic interpolants to handle conditional generation with extra control features.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper addresses the scalability and distribution modeling challenges in probabilistic time series forecasting by proposing a novel framework that blends recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with stochastic interpolants (SI). While autoregressive models like RNNs and transformers are efficient, they struggle with high-dimensional complex distributions. Conversely, generative models like diffusion and flow-based methods offer superior distribution modeling but suffer from high computational costs. The authors extend the theory of stochastic interpolants to a conditional generation framework, using an RNN to encode historical context as a prompt for the SI module. This approach allows the model to efficiently transport the current time point's distribution to the future time point's distribution, conditioned on the history. Experiments on synthetic datasets and real-world multivariate time series (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki) demonstrate that this method outperforms or matches baselines including DDPM, SGM, Flow Matching, and Vec-LSTM, particularly in capturing uncertainty and modeling complex dependencies. The study highlights the effectiveness of SI in balancing computational efficiency with high-quality probabilistic modeling.

Research Context
Autoregressive models are standard but limited in distribution complexity. Probabilistic layers are confined to simple probability families. Generative models capture complex distributions but face scalability issues. Diffusion and flow models extend to time series but are computationally heavy. Future points are close to current points, suggesting a direct mapping strategy.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can stochastic interpolants be extended for conditional time series prediction? Does blending RNN efficiency with SI modeling improve forecasting? Will conditioning on history via RNN prompts enhance generative quality? Is SI superior to DDPM, SGM, and FM for multivariate probabilistic forecasting?

Methodological Details
The study uses synthetic 2D datasets and real multivariate time series. Real datasets include Solar, Exchange, Traffic, and Wiki. Data is preprocessed following standard steps from prior literature. Performance is evaluated using CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and normalized deviance. The model learns the joint distribution of (xt+1, xt) given context. An RNN encodes the context window into a history prompt. The SI module performs conditional generation from xt to xt+1. Training utilizes importance sampling with a Beta distribution. The loss functions match velocity and score functions to theoretical targets. Inference involves recursively running step-by-step prediction.

Procedures And Architectures
The architecture combines an RNN encoder with a stochastic interpolant decoder. The RNN takes a context window of length P as input. The SI module uses velocity and score functions conditioned on the RNN output. The forward SDE is solved to generate the prediction xt+1. Hyperparameters include batch size, training epochs, and noise schedulers. Different interpolant schedules (sqrt, quad, trig) were tested. The model maps the current time point distribution to the future distribution. Training minimizes the difference between predicted and true velocity/score. The RNN output serves as the condition ξ for the generative process. The framework supports autoregressive prediction for multiple steps.

Key Results
SI achieved the lowest CRPS-sum on the Solar dataset. SI outperformed Vec-LSTM on the Solar dataset. SI performed competitively on the Exchange dataset. SI showed strong performance on the Traffic dataset. SI matched or exceeded DDPM and SGM on most metrics. FM failed to capture the Wiki data distribution. The model captured uncertainty effectively across varying scales. Synthetic results showed low Wasserstein distances for SI variants. Most gamma-interpolant combinations achieved good results. The proposed method advances generative models in time series forecasting.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The approach leverages the proximity of future to current distributions. Conditioning on history via RNN enables efficient sequential modeling. SI provides a flexible framework for conditional generation with extra features. The method bridges the gap between efficiency and distribution quality. Stochastic interpolants offer a stable alternative to learning scores directly. The framework naturally handles the transport equation between densities. Modeling the probability distribution is critical for large dimension prediction. The extension to arbitrary joint distributions broadens applicability. The continuous-time interpretation simplifies the analysis for users. The results validate the hypothesis that SI is suitable for probabilistic forecasting.

Contradictions And Limitations
Flow Matching did not yield satisfying results on real datasets. FM failed specifically on the Wiki dataset distribution. Loss values become larger when s is close to two ends. The study relies on specific interpolant schedules which may not be optimal. Code availability is pending for the camera-ready version. The method assumes continuous-time interpretation which may not fit all discrete data. The RNN context window length P is a hyperparameter that affects performance. Training stability requires importance sampling to handle integral over diffusion time. The comparison is limited to specific baselines like DDPM, SGM, FM, and Vec-LSTM. The study focuses on multivariate forecasting, potentially limiting generalizability to other tasks.

Claims
Stochastic Interpolants combined with RNNs provide a computationally efficient and high-quality framework for probabilistic time series forecasting. SI outperforms Vec-LSTM on Solar. SI matches or beats DDPM/SGM on most datasets. SI captures uncertainty well across varying scales. SI is a strong candidate for conditional generation. FM failed on the Wiki dataset. FM hyperparameter search yielded unsatisfying results. Generative models can be made scalable for time series. Distribution modeling is critical for large dimension prediction. SI offers a stable alternative to score-based models.
The proposed framework effectively extends stochastic interpolants to handle conditional generation with extra control features. The method extends SI to arbitrary joint distributions. The framework uses RNN to encode context as a prompt. The velocity and score functions depend on the condition. Loss values increase near the ends of the diffusion time. The approach simplifies the analysis for users. It enables modeling of complex dependencies.

Data And Code Availability
Synthetic datasets are from published code repositories. Real datasets are from UCI and GluonTS. Code will be publicly available in the camera-ready version.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Different interpolant schedules were tested and most worked well. Importance sampling was used to stabilize training. FM hyperparameters were searched but results were unsatisfying. The model was tested on four distinct real-world datasets. Performance was consistent across CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and ND.
